From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 22:12:03 +0000
Subject: [URGENT] Scheduler memory leak identified — proposed short-notice patch

Hi Mina, Sam,

We observed increasing memory retention on inference scheduler processes servicing CloudAtlas traffic starting ~17:00 PDT. After correlating traces and heap dumps, the on-call team identified a leak triggered by eviction logic in the scheduler under high-concurrency reroute scenarios. This has manifested as intermittent slowdowns and a handful of customer-facing 503s.

Impact: CloudAtlas saw ~0.7% request error spike and tail latency increase on large-batch workflows.
Risk assessment: Fix is low-risk (bounds to scheduler only) but requires a rolling restart of scheduler nodes per region with a tiny config bump and a hotfix binary. Estimated customer-facing window: 10–15 minutes per node; full rollout targeted within 90 minutes from approval.

Proposed action (short-notice hotfix):
- Apply hotfix binary hotfix-20261028.patch to scheduler image (non-disruptive to model payloads).
- Rolling restart with health-check gating and graceful drain.
- Monitor latency/error rates; auto-rollback if errors > 1.5x baseline within 10 minutes.

Attachments: ops-runbook-20261028.pdf (runbook), hotfix-20261028.patch (diff summary).

Requesting permission to proceed for CloudAtlas; Mina, can you confirm outreach/ask? Sam — we want to schedule a short maintenance window starting now if acceptable.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
